title: Single-degree exact-term Hom preserves quasi-isomorphisms with independent site universes
statement: Let C be a small category, J a Grothendieck topology and R a sheaf of commutative rings. Let P be a cochain complex of sheaves of R-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and fix an integer k. Assume P^n is zero for n different from k, and internal sheaf Hom from P^k preserves short exact sequences. For every quasi-isomorphism f:M to N of arbitrary cochain complexes [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], the induced map Hom(P,M) to Hom(P,N) [def-pur-hom-complex] is a quasi-isomorphism. Here the site has object universe c and morphism universe v, the commutative coefficient ring and module sheaves have universe max c v r, and the sheafification hypotheses are explicit. No equality of these universes is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, Hom products and differential; Tag 08DM, bounded Hom calculation; Tag 010N, exact functors; step 1 of lem-pc-bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso

proof.text: Let F be internal sheaf Hom from P.X k. Prove additivity by sectionwise extensionality. The hypothesis hexact says that S.map F is short exact for every short exact S; Functor.exact_tfae therefore supplies F.PreservesHomology.

Use homComplex_projections_exists to obtain the limit fan and differential and map formulas for the actual chosen Hom-complex. For p different from k, contravariant internal Hom is additive and hence carries the zero source object to zero. Projection to k is invertible: lift the family which is the identity at k and zero elsewhere; the fan universal property proves both inverse identities. This also works when P.X k is zero.

For adjacent n,m, the source differential P.d k (k+m-n) is zero since its target degree differs from k. The specified differential formula thus reduces to postcomposition with M.d (k+n) (k+m). The specified chain-map formula gives naturality with postcomposition by f in each degree. Assemble the three invertible projections into an isomorphism between the short complex at n of Hom(P,M) and F applied to the short complex of M at k+n, and similarly for N. These isomorphisms give an isomorphism of arrows.

QuasiIsoAt f (k+n) gives a quasi-isomorphism of the three-term complex at k+n. F preserves that quasi-isomorphism by ShortComplex.quasiIso_map_of_preservesLeftHomology, the natural exact-functor homology comparison. Transport through the arrow isomorphism using ShortComplex.quasiIso_iff_of_arrow_mk_iso. Apply quasiIsoAt_iff' and quasiIso_iff for all integer n. No boundedness or shift sign convention is required.

theorem quasiIso_homComplex_map_of_single_degree_exact_termOfUniverses
    {C : Type c} [Category.{v} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max c v r}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max c v r}]
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max c v r})
    (P : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj R)) ℤ)
    (k : ℤ) (hsingle : ∀ n : ℤ, n ≠ k → IsZero (P.X n))
    (hexact : ∀ (S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj R))),
      S.ShortExact → ∃ hz : SheafOfModules.homObjMap.{max c v r, v, c, max c v r} (R := R) (𝟙 (P.X
          k)) S.f ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap.{max c v r, v, c, max c v r} (R := R) (𝟙 (P.X k)) S.g = 0,
        (ShortComplex.mk (SheafOfModules.homObjMap.{max c v r, v, c, max c v r} (R := R) (𝟙 (P.X
            k)) S.f)
          (SheafOfModules.homObjMap.{max c v r, v, c, max c v r} (R := R) (𝟙 (P.X k)) S.g)
              hz).ShortExact)
    {M N : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj R)) ℤ}
    (f : M ⟶ N) [QuasiIso f] :
    QuasiIso (((homComplexFunctor.{c, v, max c v r, max c v r} (R := R)).obj (op P)).map f)
